lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for focused listening, accurate pointing to the correct school subjects and clear, confident repetition of the new words.
“Wow, look at this new noticeboard at school! It's all about our favourite subjects. I can see lots of pictures - can you tell me which subject is which?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connection. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, pencil grip and penmanship.
“I know English is your favourite subject! But if you had to choose another subject, which would it be?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - A Look and circle

details: Look and circle reinforces the unit's vocabulary by linking visual cues to the written words. Students look at each picture and circle the correct school subject to show their understanding.
Look for careful observation of the pictures and accurate circling of the corresponding subject names for each item.
“I'm trying to make labels for all my school books. Can you look at the pictures and choose the right label for each one?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer provides controlled practice of the target question and answer structure.
Look for accurate use of ‘When have you got…?’ and ‘I’ve got… on…’, correct vocabulary for subjects and days and natural turn-taking.
“Now I need to remember what book to bring on which day. Can you tell me which subject we have each day?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - D.  Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer extends the grammar practice to the third person. Students use the visual timetable to ask and answer questions about other people's schedules, building grammatical accuracy and contextual understanding.
Look for accurate use of the third-person question form (‘When has he/she…?’), correct answers based on the timetable and clear pronunciation.
“Now that we know our timetables, we can ask our friends about theirs.”

The chant consolidates the unit's grammar and vocabulary through rhythm and repetition. It allows students to practise natural intonation and sentence stress, as well as the ‘When [verb] [pronoun]’ structure, for all forms of the target question.
Look for enthusiastic participation, clear pronunciation of the different question forms and correct rhythm and clapping from the whole class.
“I’m excited to go to all our different classes this week!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
